changes: First web edition of the merged Secret Hitler + XL rulebook.
Seat counts for 17 to 19 players are experimental.

blocks.title: The original game
blocks.sub: 5 to 10 players. Everything in this part is the base game by Mike Boxleiter, Tommy Maranges and Mac Schubert, reworded but unchanged.

blocks.html: The year is 1932. The place is Germany before the war. Players are politicians trying to hold a fragile Liberal government together and stem the rising tide of Fascism. But there are secret Fascists among them, and one player is Secret Hitler.

At the start, each player is secretly given one of three roles: Liberal, Fascist or Hitler. The Liberals have a majority but do not know for sure who anyone is. The Fascists must rely on secrecy and sabotage. Hitler plays for the Fascist team. The Fascists know who Hitler is from the outset, but Hitler does not know the Fascists and must work out who they are.

rows: Five Liberal policies are enacted, or Hitler is assassinated.
Six Fascist policies are enacted, or Hitler is elected Chancellor at any time after the third Fascist policy has been enacted.

blocks.html: Whenever a Fascist policy is enacted, the government becomes more powerful: the President gets a single-use power that must be used before the next round. It does not matter which team the President is on. Even Liberal players may be tempted to enact a Fascist policy to gain a power.

blocks.caption: Policy tiles and their back, a Secret Role and its back, Party Membership cards and their back, and the two ballots.

rows: Role Briefing cards, one for each Secret Role card
Fascist boards (5-6, 7-8, 9+ players) and one Liberal board
Draw pile card and discard pile card

blocks.label: Why two cards?
blocks.html: Every player has a Secret Role card and a Party Membership card. The investigation power shows only the Party Membership card. Hitler's membership card says Fascist and gives no hint of the special role, so Liberals who uncover a Fascist must work out for themselves whether they have found an ordinary Fascist or the leader.

Choose the Fascist board for your number of players and place it next to the Liberal board. Shuffle the 11 Fascist and 6 Liberal policy tiles into one deck and place it face down on the draw pile card.

blocks.caption: The Liberal board: five policy spaces, the election tracker along the bottom, draw pile and discard pile at the ends.
A Fascist board (7 or 8 players): six policy spaces. The icon on a space is the power the President gets when a policy lands there.

blocks.html: Fill one envelope per player with a Secret Role card, its Role Briefing card, the matching Party Membership card and a ballot card, with Ja! on one side and Nein on the other. The Role Briefing card explains that role on its own, so a new player can read it at the table. Liberal roles always go with a Liberal membership card. Fascist and Hitler roles always go with a Fascist membership card. Shuffle the envelopes and deal one to each player at random. Everyone looks at their role in secret.
Choose the first presidential candidate at random and give that player both placards.

blocks.label: Dictator card
blocks.html: Some editions of the XL files include a Dictator role card. It is the same role as Hitler under another name, offered as an alternative for countries and groups where the original name is a problem. Every rule about Hitler applies to the Dictator unchanged. Use one or the other, never both.

blocks.title: 5 or 6 players
lines: Everybody close your eyes.
Fascist and Hitler, open your eyes and acknowledge each other.
[Take a long pause]
Everyone close your eyes.
Everyone can open your eyes. If anyone is confused or something went wrong, please tell the group now.

blocks.title: 7 to 10 players
lines: Everybody close your eyes and extend your hand into a fist in front of you.
All Fascists who are not Hitler, open your eyes and acknowledge each other.
Hitler, keep your eyes closed but put your thumb out.
Fascists, take note of who has an extended thumb. That player is Hitler.
[Take a long pause]
Everyone close your eyes and put your hands down.
Everyone can open your eyes. If anyone is confused or something went wrong, please tell the group now.

blocks.html: The game is played in rounds. Each round has an Election to form a government, a Legislative Session to enact a new policy, and an Executive Action to use a power, if one was unlocked.

items: Pass the presidency. The President placard moves clockwise to the next player, who is the new presidential candidate.
Nominate a Chancellor. The candidate passes the Chancellor placard to any other eligible player. The candidate may discuss the options with the table.
Vote. When everyone is ready, every player, including both candidates, hides their ballot card in their hands, then at the same moment lays it down with Ja! or Nein facing up.

blocks.caption: Example with seven players: four Ja!, three Nein. A majority voted yes, so the government is elected. Three against three with one player dead would be a tie, and a tie fails.

items: The last elected President and the last elected Chancellor are term-limited and cannot be nominated as Chancellor.
Term limits follow the last pair elected, not the last pair nominated.
Term limits affect only the chancellorship. Anyone can be President, even the player who was just Chancellor.
If only five players are left in the game, only the last elected Chancellor is barred; the last President may be nominated.

blocks.html: A tie or a majority of Nein means the vote fails. The candidate misses the chance to be President, the placard moves clockwise to the next player, and the election tracker advances one step.

blocks.label: Election tracker
blocks.html: If the group rejects three governments in a row, the country falls into chaos. Reveal the policy on top of the deck and enact it at once. Any power it would grant is ignored. Existing term limits are forgotten, so every player is eligible as Chancellor in the next election. If fewer than three tiles remain in the deck at that point, shuffle them with the discard pile into a new deck. The tracker resets whenever any policy is placed face up, by a government or by chaos.

The candidates become President and Chancellor. If three or more Fascist policies are already enacted, ask whether the new Chancellor is Hitler. If so, the game is over and the Fascists win. If not, everyone now knows for sure that this player is not Hitler. Then go to the legislative session.

items: The President draws the top three tiles, looks at them in secret and discards one face down.
The other two go to the Chancellor, who looks in secret, discards one face down and enacts the last one face up on the matching board.

steps.title: The President
steps.html: draws three tiles and discards one, face down.

steps.title: The Chancellor
steps.html: receives the other two and discards one, face down.

steps.title: Enacted
steps.html: The last tile goes face up on its board.

blocks.caption: Example: the President draws Fascist, Fascist, Liberal. Had the President been a Fascist, the Liberal tile could have been the one discarded, and nobody else would know.

items: The President hands both tiles over at the same time, not one by one.
No talking and no signals between President and Chancellor during the session.
Neither may pick at random, shuffle the tiles first or use any other trick to avoid deliberately choosing a policy.
Discarded tiles are never shown. The table must rely on the word of the President and the Chancellor, who are free to lie.
If fewer than three tiles remain in the deck at the end of a session, shuffle them with the discard pile into a new deck. Do not reveal the leftover tiles and do not simply put them on top.

blocks.html: If the enacted Fascist policy covered a presidential power, the sitting President uses it now. If a Liberal policy was enacted, or a Fascist policy with no power, start a new round.

The President must use the power before the next round can begin. The President may discuss it with other players first, but decides alone how and when it is used. Powers are used once. They do not stack or roll over to later turns.

items.name: Investigate Loyalty
items.html: Chooses a player to investigate. That player hands over the Party Membership card, not the Secret Role card. The President checks it in secret and returns it, and may share or lie about the result. No player may be investigated twice in the same game.

items.name: Call Special Election
items.html: Chooses any other player as the next presidential candidate by passing the President placard, even to a term-limited player. That player nominates a Chancellor and the election proceeds as usual. Afterwards the placard returns to the left of the President who called it.

items.name: Policy Peek
items.html: Secretly looks at the top three tiles of the deck and returns them without changing the order.

items.name: Execution
items.html: Executes one player by saying “I formally execute” and the player’s name. If that player is Hitler, the game ends in a Liberal victory. If not, the table does not learn whether a Fascist or a Liberal was killed. Executed players may not speak, vote or run for office.

items.name: Execution + Veto
items.html: The fifth Fascist space. The President executes a player, as above, and from now on the veto power is unlocked for every government until the end of the game.

blocks.html: The veto comes into effect after five Fascist policies have been enacted and stays for the rest of the game. The President draws three tiles, discards one and passes two as usual. The Chancellor may then, instead of enacting, say "I wish to veto this agenda." If the President consents by saying "I agree to the veto," both tiles are discarded and the President placard passes on. If the President does not consent, the Chancellor must enact a policy as normal. Each veto is an inactive government and advances the election tracker by one.

Players often learn things the rest of the table does not know: what tiles the government saw, or what an investigation showed. You may always lie about hidden knowledge. The only time a player must tell the truth is in the game-ending Hitler situations: a player who is Hitler must say so if assassinated, or if elected Chancellor after three Fascist policies.

items: Everyone should claim to be a Liberal. The Liberal majority can shut out anyone who admits to being a Fascist. Liberals should usually tell the truth; they are solving a puzzle, and lying hurts their own team.

Hitler should be as Liberal as possible. Enact Liberal policies, vote for Liberal governments, and let the other Fascists create openings. Fascists win by quiet manipulation, not by playing openly evil.
Liberals gain from slowing down and discussing what is known. Fascists gain from rushed votes and confusion.
Fascists most often win by electing Hitler, not by six policies. It is the core of their strategy, so Hitler needs the Liberals' trust when the time comes.
Ask players to explain their actions, above all with powers. Ask a candidate in advance whom they would investigate, appoint or execute.
When a Fascist policy appears, there are only three possible culprits: the President, the Chancellor or the deck.

blocks.title: Secret Hitler XL
blocks.sub: 6 to 19 players. The fan expansion by Bo-Jivan Parker (Lord_Roguy): a Communist party, thirteen extra roles, emergency powers and anti-policies. Use Part One for everything not changed here.

blocks.html: XL is a kit of modules. Every part is optional; the table shows when each one is worth adding.

rows: A third hidden party with its own board, policies and powers.
Always. This is what makes XL.
Ten one-shot policies that give the President an extra power.
Thirteen roles with their own powers and goals.
Policies that remove a rival policy and help the Liberals.

blocks.html: Each envelope holds three cards, plus the ballot card (Ja! on one side, Nein on the other). The Secret Role card says who you are. The Role Briefing card explains, on its own, how that role wins, what it knows and what it can do. The Party Membership card is what investigations see.

blocks.caption: A Communist's envelope: Secret Role, Role Briefing, Party Membership, and both sides of the ballot card.
Counts for 6 to 16 players are from the XL rules. 17 to 19 players are experimental; those counts and the emergency tiles follow the separate Rulings and balance notes sheet.

items: Fascist board: by player count, as in the original game: 5-6, 7-8 or 9+ players.
Communist board: one board for every player count.
Who knows whom: the Communists always know each other. Hitler knows the Fascists only when there is exactly one Fascist.

rows: Spare membership deck: 2 Liberal, 1 Fascist, 1 Communist
The Detective, if that role plays

blocks.html: Read it aloud at setup. Lines marked with a role are read only when that role is in the game. Fascists here means the Fascist roles, the Bodyguard, the Fascist Spy, and a Propagandist, Bureaucrat or Detective holding a Fascist card: never Hitler, the Monarchist or the Jester.

blocks.title: Night script for Secret Hitler XL
lines: Everybody close your eyes and hold a fist out in front of you.
Only with the Detective: Detective, open your eyes. Take the top card of the spare membership deck: you now belong to that party. Put it in your envelope and close your eyes.
Fascists, except Hitler and the Monarchist, open your eyes and recognise each other.
Hitler, put your thumb out. Fascists, this is Hitler. Hitler, put your thumb away. (With only one Fascist, Hitler opens their eyes with them instead.)
Only with the Monarchist: Monarchist, put your thumb out. Fascists, this is the Monarchist. Monarchist, put your thumb away.
Fascists, close your eyes.
Only with the Spies: Liberal Spy, open your eyes. Fascists, put your thumbs out. [Pause] Thumbs away. Liberal Spy, close your eyes.

Communists, open your eyes and recognise each other. Only with the Anarchist: Anarchist, put your thumb out (with only one other Communist, open your eyes instead). Thumb away. Communists, close your eyes.
Only with Centrists: Centrists, open your eyes, recognise each other, close your eyes.
Everybody put your hands down and open your eyes.

blocks.label: How long is a big game?
blocks.html: The Communist board adds up to five more governments. From 11 players, emergency tiles stretch the game further, so that most players get a turn as President.

blocks.caption: Two Communist roles, the Communist Party Membership card and a Communist policy.

blocks.html: The Communists are a third party with their own policies and their own board. Communist roles go with Communist Party Membership cards. Communist policies are shuffled into the deck and enacted like any other policy, onto the Communist board. The Communists know each other from the start.

items: Their board is full of Communist policies.
Hitler is executed. Then Communists and Liberals win together.

blocks.caption: The Communist board: Bugging, Radicalisation, Five-year plan, Congress, Confession, then the winning space.

blocks.html: A Communist power is triggered when a Communist policy lands on its space, whoever the government is. Radicalisation and Congress are carried out by the Communists while everyone else has their eyes closed; a small closed-eye icon in the corner of the space marks them. The Anarchist never opens their eyes for these.

items.name: Bugging
items.html: No eyes are closed. The President and the Chancellor together look at one player's Party Membership card. The Capitalist chooses which of their two cards to show.

items.name: Radicalisation
items.html: The Communists try to turn another player into a Communist. Fascists cannot be radicalised, and neither can a player whose card was already investigated by a Fascist-board power.

items.name: Five-year plan
items.html: Shuffle two Communist policies and one Liberal policy from the reserve into the draw deck.

items.name: Congress
items.html: The newly radicalised Communists learn who the original Communists are.

items.name: Confession
items.html: The President executes a player of their choice. That player reveals their Party Membership card to everyone.

blocks.title: Radicalisation
lines: Everyone not yet investigated by a Fascist-board power, take out your Party Membership card and place it face down in front of you. Capitalist, put out your Fascist card.
Everyone close your eyes.
Communists, open your eyes and look at one player's card together.
If it is a Liberal card, swap it for a spare Communist card and put the old card in the centre. If it is a Fascist card, put it back: the attempt fails.
Communists, close your eyes.
Only with the Capitalist: Capitalist, open your eyes. Place the Lobby card on the card of the player you trust most. Close your eyes.
Everyone reach out and move your card around slightly.
Everyone open your eyes and check your card. If it has been swapped, you are now a Communist and win only if the Communists win.

blocks.title: Congress
lines: Everyone close your eyes.
Communists, open your eyes and recognise each other.
Communists, close your eyes.
Everyone open your eyes.

blocks.html: Each extra role takes the seat of a regular role, and its player gets that role's own Role Briefing card. The briefing explains everything the player needs, so this chapter is mostly for the person who sets up the game.

rows: Big games: the Liberals get a small group that trusts each other.
Communist policies pass too quickly, or Radicalisation is too easy.
The group knows the Communists well and wants a wild card.
Hitler is found and executed too often.
You want a hidden duel. Always add both.
Liberals are fooled about discards too often.
A Liberal; party drawn at setup

blocks.label: Advice
blocks.html: With the Communists, add only Centrists, the Capitalist, the Monarchist and the Anarchist, and only above 10 players. The other roles suit games without Communists. Start with one extra role at a time.

Big games need more chances to investigate and execute, and they need to last longer. Emergency tiles give both. An enacted emergency tile is not placed on any board: it leaves the game, and the President uses the power printed on it. Shuffle the ten tiles face down and add 7 of them to the deck at 11 to 14 players, all 10 from 15 players.

items.name: Investigate Loyalty
items.html: The President looks at one player's Party Membership card.

items.name: Policy Peek
items.html: The President secretly looks at the top three policies and puts them back in order.

items.name: Special Election
items.html: The President picks the next presidential candidate.

items.name: Execution
items.html: The President executes a player.

items.name: Propaganda
items.html: The President looks at the top policy, then puts it back or discards it.

items.name: No Confidence
items.html: Veto power is unlocked for the next government only.

items.name: Censorship
items.html: The next government has no Chancellor: the next elected President draws three, discards two and enacts one.

items.name: Enabling Act
items.html: The next time a President gets a presidential power, their Chancellor uses it instead.

items.name: Article 48
items.html: The President uses any presidential or emergency power of their choice, except Execution.

items.name: Pardon
items.html: The President investigates a player's Party Membership card, even one who was investigated before.

blocks.html: Each anti-policy replaces a tile already in the deck: Anti-Fascist replaces a Communist policy, Anti-Communist a Fascist policy, Social Democratic a Liberal policy. They lengthen the game and help the Liberals most.

items.name: Anti-Communist
items.html: Goes on the Fascist board. The President uses the power of that space. Then one Communist policy moves from the Communist board to the discard pile, and that Communist power is not used a second time.

items.name: Anti-Fascist
items.html: Goes on the Communist board. The Communist power of that space is used. Then one Fascist policy moves from the Fascist board to the discard pile, and that presidential power is not used a second time.

items.name: Social Democratic
items.html: Goes on the Liberal board. On the count of three, the President and the Chancellor each name a policy type. If they match, one tile of that type leaves the draw deck for good. Then shuffle the draw deck, without the discard pile.

blocks.html: Every side and every extra role has its own way to win. Find yours below; your Role Briefing card says the same.

panels.name: Liberals
items: The Liberal board is full.
Hitler is executed.

panels.name: Fascists
items: The Fascist board is full.
Hitler is elected Chancellor after the 3rd Fascist policy.
A Fascist-team player executes the Liberal Spy.

panels.name: Communists
items: The Communist board is full.
Hitler is executed (together with the Liberals).

panels.name: Monarchist
items: The Fascist board is full.
Hitler is executed.
Never when Hitler becomes Chancellor.

panels.name: Jester
items: The Jester is executed: the game ends and nobody else wins.

panels.name: Card-party roles
items: The party on their Party Membership card wins.

blocks.label: When Hitler is executed
blocks.html: Liberals, Communists and the Monarchist win together. A Bodyguard who is still alive dies instead, once, and the game goes on.

rows: The President placard moves clockwise. The candidate nominates a Chancellor; the last elected President and Chancellor are barred. Everyone votes Ja! or Nein. A majority of Ja! elects the government.
The election tracker advances. After three failed votes the top policy is enacted with no power, and term limits are forgotten.
Ask every newly elected Chancellor whether they are Hitler. If so, the Fascists win.
The President draws three tiles and discards one. The Chancellor gets two, discards one and enacts the last. No talking. Reshuffle when fewer than three tiles remain.
If the new policy covered a power, the President uses it now.
After five Fascist policies (or for one government after No Confidence) the Chancellor may ask to veto; if the President agrees, both tiles are discarded and the tracker advances.
The President looks at one Party Membership card. Once per player.
The President picks the next presidential candidate; then the order resumes.
The President looks at the top three tiles.
The President kills a player. If it is Hitler, the Liberals win.
The President and Chancellor look at one Party Membership card.
The Communists turn a Liberal into a Communist. Fascists cannot be radicalised.
Shuffle 2 Communist and 1 Liberal policy into the deck.
New Communists learn who the original Communists are.
The President executes a player, whose Party Membership card is revealed.
